text:
A: Hiya! Oh, can you hear me alright? I'm Gemma.
B: Yeah, fine. Tariq. Hi.
A: Hi Tariq. Erm, so, did you do that puzzle thing at the start? I was useless, I'm not gonna lie, I got about three and then sort of just stared at it.
B: The pattern ones? Yeah. Some of the later ones were a bit ambiguous, I thought. Two of them had more than one defensible answer.
A: Oh, that makes me feel better actually! I thought it was just me. So what do you do, if you don't mind me asking?
B: I run operations for a facilities management company. Office cleaning, security, maintenance, that kind of thing, across London. So about forty contracts, five site managers, and a lot of people ringing me when a lift breaks.
A: Forty! Blimey. That sounds really stressful, is it?
B: It can be. Had a client ring at nine o'clock last night about a lift. It's fine. Most of it's just catching problems before the client does. What about you?
A: Erm, so, I'm a dog groomer, well, assistant dog groomer, two days a week in Walsall. So bathing, drying, nails, and I'm learning the proper cuts off my boss. And I'm doing a psychology degree with the Open University, which is sort of the main thing really, I want to go into mental health eventually. That's probably more than you asked, sorry!
B: No, that's fine. Open University, part-time? Evenings?
A: Yeah, evenings mostly. Second year.
B: Respect for that, honestly. I did my CIMA part-time while I was working. Accountancy qualification. Took me years. It's the evenings that kill you, right, you come in knackered and then you've got to sit down and do another three hours.
A: Yes! That's exactly it. And I've got a dog snoring on the settee downstairs which doesn't help, I can hear him from here. Did you, like, did you find it got easier?
B: Not easier. You just get more disciplined about it. I blocked out the same nights every week and didn't move them. If you leave it to how you feel, you won't do it.
A: Same nights every week. Yeah, that's probably where I'm going wrong, I sort of do it when there's a deadline, do you know what I mean?
B: Everyone does. How are your marks?
A: Erm, decent actually. Better than I thought. I always think I'm not clever enough for it and then the mark comes back and it's fine.
B: Then you're clever enough for it. That's what the marks are for.
A: Ha, that's fair. I'll tell myself that. Are you in London then, like, central?
B: Gants Hill. Ilford. Live with my parents, actually, in the house I grew up in.
A: Oh, me too! I moved back in with my mum and dad a couple of years ago. I'm always a bit embarrassed saying it, at thirty-five.
B: I'm forty. Don't be embarrassed. Dad's getting older, someone's got to be there. My mum still thinks I work too much, mind.
A: That's my dad! I worry about him, he won't go the doctor's for anything. Sunday dinner's my mum's thing though, that's sacred in our house.
B: Sundays my sister comes round with her three kids. It's chaos. Good chaos.
A: Aw. I've got two nieces, I do their hair for school plays and that. Do you do anything outside work, or is it all lifts and spreadsheets?
B: Badminton on Wednesdays, cycling Saturdays. And I read a lot. History, mostly. Cities, architecture.
A: Ooh, I do Zumba on Wednesdays! Not the same, is it.
B: Not really, no.
A: Ha! Fair. Is there a place you'd most like to... sorry, a place you've been that you'd sort of recommend?
B: Samarkand. Uzbekistan. The Registan. If you ever get the chance, honestly, the tilework alone is worth the...
